report.summary: Independent read-only review of SwiftSpim (all production Swift sources, Package.swift, scripts, tests partially, README/usermanual/COMPATIBILITY/MACOS-VALIDATION/notices/Info.plist) against SPIM/QtSpim r764 in ../Reference/spimsimulator-code-r764. Nothing was built or run; every finding comes from reading the code and is cross-checked against upstream source lines. The core is careful in many areas. These were checked and found to match upstream, so they are not reported: MMIO decoding regardless of -mapped_io, delayed-load clobbering in ldc1, sc not writing rt, CTC1/FP-compare FPE behavior, kernel-text loads raising DBE, text-segment byte stores to empty words, branch-likely nullification, and the byte-identical bundled exceptions.s. The most significant defects: (1) the recovering assembler stops assembling the rest of a file after upstream-recoverable semantic errors such as duplicate labels, data in .text, $32, MIPS32r2 ops, or div-by-zero constants, which silently changes the program; (2) the GUI run loop caps simulation at about 85k instructions/s; (3) a non-.globl label in a later-loaded file does not satisfy an earlier file's forward reference, unlike upstream; (4) a breakpoint on an input syscall fires a second time after input is supplied; (5) exception and warning messages that upstream prints (with -quiet honored) are never produced, and the comparison harness hides this by passing -quiet only to the oracle; (6) appending a file to a started session silently resets the heap, grown stack, open files, pending input, delay-slot state and self-modified code; (7) non-UTF-8 bytes in program output, input and source are replaced or rejected; (8) a relocated CLI crashes via Bundle.module fatalError. Full parity is not achieved. The documentation is mostly honest about gaps, but some claims are broader than the evidence ("compares stderr", "file I/O as in QtSpim").

findings.title: Recovering assembler stops assembling the rest of the file on semantic errors that upstream reports and continues past
findings.line: 228-234 (catch + unlabeled break exits the per-line loop); throw sites 312, 544, 566, 678, 757, 772, 1073
findings.trigger:
Load in the GUI or CLI (both use recovering: true) a file whose line 3 repeats a label, e.g. `.data
x: .word 1
x: .word 2
.text
.globl main
main: li $v0,10
syscall`. The same happens with `.asciiz` in .text, `$32`, a MIPS32r2 op such as `seb`, `break 1`, or `div $t0,$t1,0`.
findings.actual: The AssemblyError is appended to diagnostics, then `break` leaves the whole `for (index, raw) in lines` loop, so every later line of the file is dropped. In the example `main` is never defined and the run ends with "Instruction references undefined symbol" from __start's `jal main`.
findings.expected: Upstream yyerror() only sets parse_error_occurred and prints (parser.y:2941-2946); the line still finishes via LINE_PARSE_DONE=YYACCEPT (parser.y:455), and read_assembly_file loops `while (!yyparse())` (spim-utils.cpp:180-181). Only a real grammar syntax error ends the file. Duplicate labels (sym-tbl.cpp:164), data in text (parser.y:2117 etc.), register range (parser.y:2525), break 1 (parser.y:845), divide by zero (parser.y:1105) and Rev2 'Instruction ignored' (parser.y:2959) all continue.
findings.evidence: Swift `break` inside a catch clause targets the enclosing for-loop. testRecoveringSyntaxErrorStopsOnlyTheCurrentInput (AssemblerParityTests.swift:138-146) codifies this for a real syntax error, but no test covers semantic errors.
findings.suggested_resolution: Split diagnostics into syntax (stop the current input) and semantic (record, clear the current line's labels as clear_labels does, continue with the next line). Map each upstream yyerror site to the continue path. For Rev2 ops, emit nothing and keep going.
findings.validation: Add XCTests for each semantic-error class checking that later labels and instructions exist. Add a compare-upstream fixture with a duplicate label followed by a valid program and compare stdout, stderr and status.

findings.title: GUI run loop sleeps 12 ms after every 1,024 instructions, capping speed at about 85k instructions/s
findings.trigger: Run in the app any program that executes about 10M instructions, such as nested loops or bubble sort on a few thousand elements.
findings.actual: Throughput cannot exceed about 1024/0.012 ≈ 85k instr/s even before simulation cost, so 10M instructions take about 2 minutes or more. CP0 Count still advances by wall clock (Machine.swift:346-356), so timer programs see one tick every ~850 instructions instead of every few million.
findings.expected: QtSpim runs 100,000-instruction batches and only calls processEvents in between (menu.cpp:265-276), running coursework at native interpreter speed.
findings.evidence: Code reading only; no timing was measured in this review.
findings.suggested_resolution: Use a time-sliced budget: run until about 8-16 ms of wall time has passed, then `await Task.yield()` instead of sleeping. Alternatively move execution to a dedicated actor or thread with snapshots published to the main actor. Keep the UI refresh throttling.
findings.validation: Add a benchmark fixture (e.g. a 50M-iteration loop) and record GUI wall time against the CLI. Add a timer.s/time.s run comparing interrupt counts per instruction.

findings.title: Forward reference in one file to a non-.globl label defined in a later-loaded file stays undefined
findings.line: 190-214 (pre-pass marks every file-defined label local), 140-145 (key), 237-263 (fixups resolved before scoped labels are published)
findings.trigger: Load a.s (`.globl main; main: jal helper; li $v0,10; syscall`), then load b.s (`helper: jr $ra`, no .globl), in the GUI or in one CLI/test assembly.
findings.actual: b.s stores helper under the scoped key "2\u{1f}helper", so a.s's fixup for "helper" fails. unresolvedSymbols contains helper, and helper is then added to image.symbols at lines 259-263, so the Symbols dialog lists it while execution faults with "Instruction references undefined symbol".
findings.expected: Upstream creates a label entry on first use (lookup_label, sym-tbl.cpp:134-154). A later definition fills in that same entry (record_label, 159-179) and clear_labels resolves the recorded uses (parser.y:2699-2704; sym-tbl.cpp:221-235). flush_local_labels runs afterwards (sym-tbl.cpp:334-356). The earlier file's reference therefore resolves.
findings.evidence: Source reading of both implementations; no runtime confirmation in this review.
findings.suggested_resolution: Model upstream's single table plus flush: when a file defines a local label whose name has unresolved global-key uses from earlier inputs, resolve those uses to it before the label becomes file-local.
findings.validation: Add an XCTest with the a.s/b.s pair: expect no unresolved symbols and halted(0). Add the reverse load order to confirm it stays undefined, as upstream.

findings.title: Breakpoint on an input syscall fires again after the user supplies input
findings.line: 195-204 (breakpointSkip cleared before execute), 392-400 (waitingInput returns without advancing pc); Sources/SwiftSpim/Debugger.swift 316, 328-330, 369-381
findings.trigger: Set a breakpoint on the `syscall` of read_int (v0=5) and press Run. At the breakpoint press Continue, then type a number in the Console and press Send.
findings.actual: Continue sets breakpointSkip=nil, then execute() sees no input and returns .waitingInput with pc still at the breakpoint. sendInput → provideInput (.paused) → run() → Machine.run sees breakpoints.contains(pc) && breakpointSkip(nil) != pc and stops again, showing a second 'Breakpoint Reached'.
findings.expected: In QtSpim the syscall blocks inside read_input (spim_support.cpp:111-127; syscall.cpp:130-136), so once the breakpoint is continued the instruction completes without stopping again (menu.cpp:377-384).
findings.evidence: Control flow traced through Machine.run, Machine.execute and Debugger.sendInput/run.
findings.suggested_resolution: Keep breakpointSkip set when execute() returns .waitingInput (only clear it after the instruction actually retires), or have provideInput keep the skip for the waiting pc.
findings.validation: Core test: breakpoint on the read syscall, run → paused, run → waitingInput, provideInput, run → must reach halted without another pause at that pc. Also cover the Debugger.sendInput path in a UI or unit test.

findings.title: No 'Exception occurred at PC=…' messages, and -quiet has no effect; the parity harness hides the gap
findings.trigger: Run `li $t0,0x7fffffff; addi $t0,$t0,1` with the default handler, in the CLI without -quiet or in the GUI with Quiet off.
findings.actual: Only the guest handler's console text appears. No message is written to stderr (CLI) or Messages (GUI), and Quiet/-quiet controls nothing in the core.
findings.expected: Upstream handle_exception writes 'Exception occurred at PC=0x%08x' plus a reason (e.g. '  Arithmetic overflow') through error() unless quiet (syscall.cpp:241-299). The terminal error() writes to stderr (spim.cpp:860-871). QtSpim appends to Messages and shows a dialog (spim_support.cpp:60-69; spimview.cpp:268-284). -bare sets quiet (spim.cpp:172; QtSpim main.cpp:141).
findings.evidence: compare-upstream.sh passes -quiet only to the reference (line 19) and runs the Swift CLI without it (line 20). The 'stderr matches' claim (COMPATIBILITY.md:26, 34) therefore holds only for quiet mode.
findings.suggested_resolution: Add an exception-message callback or log to Machine that mirrors handle_exception text, gated by a quiet option. Route it to stderr in the CLI and to Messages (optionally an alert) in the GUI. Run both sides of the harness with the same flags and add one non-quiet case.
findings.validation: compare-upstream with and without -quiet on an overflow/trap fixture; expect byte-identical stderr.

findings.title: Appending a file to a started session silently resets heap, grown stack, open files, input, delay state and self-modified code
findings.trigger: Run a program that calls sbrk and/or opens a file and grows the stack, pause it, then File → Load File… another source (keepState path).
findings.actual: A new Machine is built. Only GPRs, cp0, fcsr, FPRs, pc, hi/lo, breakpoints, output and unchanged data bytes are copied. These are reset or lost: heap and stackBottom (recomputed in reset, so sbrk'd or deeply grown memory is unmapped and raises exception 7), open guest files (FileHandles closed), queued console input, pendingBranch/pendingLoad (a pause in a delay slot loses the branch), waitingInput status, coprocessor0Control/floatingControl, MMIO and timer state, and runtime text-segment writes (code is rebuilt from the image).
findings.expected: QtSpim's Load File assembles the new file into the existing world without reinitializing memory or registers (menu.cpp:64-84; read_assembly_file, spim-utils.cpp:170-188).
findings.evidence: Machine.reset() recomputes heap/stackBottom (Machine.swift:91-97) and code from the image (80-81); none of the state above is transferred.
findings.suggested_resolution: Prefer an incremental-assembly API that patches the live Machine (add text, data and symbols; resolve fixups) instead of replacing it. Otherwise transfer all machine state, including heap, stackBottom, files, input, pending delay state and modified code.
findings.validation: Test: sbrk 64 KiB beyond the initial heap, write a word there, append-load a trivial file, read it back with no exception. Also cover open-file and delay-slot survival.

findings.title: Program output and input are forced through UTF-8 String decoding, corrupting non-UTF-8 and split multibyte bytes
findings.line: 714 (emit decodes each syscall's bytes as UTF-8), 819 (print_char), 851 (write to fd 1/2); Sources/SpimCLI/main.swift 139-140, 150-152, 160
findings.trigger: `li $a0,0xE9; li $v0,11; syscall`, or print a UTF-8 string one character at a time with syscall 11 (bytes C3 then A9).
findings.actual: Each emit decodes on its own, so a lone 0xE9 or a split sequence becomes U+FFFD. The CLI then writes EF BF BD instead of the guest bytes. CLI input via readLine and mapped-input chunk decoding also repairs or alters invalid or split UTF-8 bytes.
findings.expected: Upstream writes raw bytes ('%c', syscall.cpp:168-170; vfprintf in spim.cpp:908-939) and reads raw bytes (spim.cpp:943-969). CLI stdout byte parity is part of the compatibility claim.
findings.evidence: String(decoding:as:UTF8.self) per call at Machine.swift:714; FileHandle.standardOutput.write(Data(machine.output.utf8)) at main.swift:151.
findings.suggested_resolution: Keep console output and input as [UInt8] in Machine. Decode for display only in the GUI, buffering incomplete sequences (QtSpim itself uses Latin-1 for single chars). Make the CLI write and read raw bytes.
findings.validation: CLI fixtures printing 0x80-0xFF bytes and a char-by-char UTF-8 string, compared byte-exact against the r764 CLI; test with non-UTF-8 stdin.

findings.title: Source files that are not valid UTF-8 are refused entirely
findings.trigger: Load a .s file saved as Windows-1252 or Latin-1 with an accented character in a comment or string (common from Windows editors).
findings.actual: String(contentsOf:encoding:.utf8) throws, nothing is loaded, and an error alert or exit 1 results.
findings.expected: Upstream opens the file with fopen and scans bytes (spim-utils.cpp:171-181), so comments assemble untouched and string bytes are stored as-is.
findings.evidence: Code reading.
findings.suggested_resolution: Read Data and decode tolerantly (try UTF-8, fall back to ISO-8859-1 byte-preserving decoding), keeping string-literal bytes exact.
findings.validation: Fixture with a Latin-1 comment and `.asciiz` containing 0xE9; expect a successful load and the exact data byte.

findings.title: A relocated CLI (or other SpimCore client without the resource bundle) crashes via Bundle.module fatalError; a missing handler fails silently
findings.trigger: Copy .build/release/swiftspim-cli alone to another directory (e.g. /usr/local/bin) and run `swiftspim-cli -file helloworld.s` with the default handler.
findings.actual: If <exe dir>/SwiftSpim_SpimCore.bundle is absent, the `?? Bundle.module` fallback runs SwiftPM's accessor, which calls fatalError("unable to find bundle named SwiftSpim_SpimCore") (generated resource_bundle_accessor.swift:44). If the bundle exists but exceptions.s is unreadable, `try?` silently drops the handler and the program starts at `main` (Machine.swift:98) with no exception handling and no diagnostic.
findings.expected: Upstream reports 'Cannot read exception handler' and stops (spim-utils.cpp:111-112).
findings.evidence: Generated accessor fatalError; build-app.sh copies the bundle only for the .app.
findings.suggested_resolution: Embed exceptions.s as a Swift string constant (it is small and BSD-licensed, already in the notices), or locate the bundle without Bundle.module and throw a diagnostic when it is missing.
findings.validation: Script: copy the CLI binary alone to a temp directory and run hello world; expect success or a clean error message, not a trap.

findings.title: Bare mode forces delayed branches and loads in the core; bare without delays cannot be configured, unlike QtSpim
findings.line: 216-217; Sources/SpimCore/Assembler.swift 702; Sources/SwiftSpim/DebugDialogs.swift 136-140; listing uses only delayedBranches at DebugPanels.swift 127 and Debugger.swift 484
findings.trigger: Use QtSpim-style settings with bare machine checked and delayed branches/loads unchecked (QtSpim settings checkboxes are independent: menu.cpp:407-428, 502-506), or persisted defaults bare=true, branchDelay=false.
findings.actual: The Swift core always delays when bareMachine is set. The Preferences toggles are disabled in bare mode. If such defaults exist, the Text listing computes branch targets without the delay while execution uses it.
findings.expected: Upstream execution and branch encoding use only delayed_branches/delayed_loads (run.cpp:104-160; sym-tbl.cpp:264); bare_machine does not imply them.
findings.evidence: Upstream grep shows no bare_machine use in the delay logic.
findings.suggested_resolution: Use options.delayedBranches/delayedLoads directly. Keep the Simple/Bare buttons as presets and enable the individual toggles.
findings.validation: Unit test: bareMachine=true, delayedBranches=false; branch encoding and execution should match the upstream CLI run with -bare plus a modified build, or reasoned expected words.

findings.title: Transmitter-ready interrupt is re-raised every poll instead of on the ready transition
findings.trigger: Mapped I/O with transmitter interrupt enable set and nothing more to send. The handler clears Cause (the default handler does `mtc0 $0 $13`) and returns.
findings.actual: Every 100 instructions pollDevices sets IP10 again while ready && enabled, so the interrupt fires repeatedly.
findings.expected: Upstream raises TRANS_INT only when the buffer becomes ready or when interrupts are enabled on a ready device (mem.cpp:538-549, 556-564). A cleared Cause bit stays clear.
findings.evidence: Source comparison only; not exercised by tt.io in this review.
findings.suggested_resolution: Raise IP10 only on the busy→ready edge, plus on enable-while-ready as Machine.swift:290-291 already does.
findings.validation: Interrupt-driven output fixture counting handler entries, compared with the r764 CLI under -mapped_io.

findings.title: At stdin EOF the CLI supplies a synthetic "\n" to blocking reads
findings.trigger: Pipe a short input file and have the program call read_string or read(fd 0) after EOF.
findings.actual: read_string stores "\n\0" and read(0,…) returns 1 with '\n'. Programs that loop until EOF never see EOF and run until the 10M step budget.
findings.expected: Upstream read() returns 0, so read_input yields an empty string (spim.cpp:954-966) and the read syscall returns 0 (syscall.cpp:198-208).
findings.evidence: Code reading.
findings.suggested_resolution: Add an end-of-input flag to Machine so pending syscalls complete with empty data (read returns 0, read_int returns 0, read_char returns '\n' per syscall.cpp:176).
findings.validation: CLI fixtures reading past EOF, compared with r764 stdout and status.

findings.title: Upstream assembler diagnostics are missing or semantics differ: $at use, .repeat/.struct warnings, fatal .err
findings.line: 627-634 (noAT set but never consulted; .repeat/.struct silently ignored), 630 (.err)
findings.trigger: `addu $1,$2,$3` without `.set noat`; `.repeat 3`; `.err`.
findings.actual: No 'Register 1 is reserved for assembler' warning (noAT is unused); .repeat/.struct are silently ignored; .err becomes an ordinary recoverable diagnostic.
findings.expected: parser.y:2526-2527 warns on $1 when not bare and noat is off; 2285-2288 and 2341-2344 print 'Warning: … directive ignored'; 2213-2216 calls fatal_error.
findings.evidence: grep shows noAT referenced only at Assembler.swift:132, 219, 628-629.
findings.suggested_resolution: Emit the matching warnings via warn(); treat .err as fatal for the load.
findings.validation: Diagnostic-text tests compared with r764 stderr output.

findings.title: Entry point falls back to `main` or the lowest text address when __start is absent; missing-handler fault text differs
findings.trigger: Run with -noexception on a program that defines only main.
findings.actual: Execution starts at main, and the eventual `jr $ra` to 0 is reported as 'MIPS exception 6 at 0x00000000'.
findings.expected: Upstream starts only at __start (spim-utils.cpp:190-192; spim.cpp:295). Without it PC=0, which leads to IBE → 0x80000180 → 'Attempt to execute non-instruction at 0x80000180' (run.cpp:229-237).
findings.evidence: Code comparison.
findings.suggested_resolution: Match upstream entry selection (allowing an explicit option for the lenient behavior). With no handler, jump to 0x80000180 and report the upstream non-instruction message.
findings.validation: CLI comparison of -noexception with a main-only program.

findings.title: Guest stack has no host environment strings (envp empty) and a different initial $sp
findings.trigger: A program walking envp ($a2), or printing initial $sp/argv addresses.
findings.actual: envp is an empty vector and strings start at 0x7fffffff with only argv.
findings.expected: initialize_run_stack copies every environ entry before argv and builds the envp vector (spim-utils.cpp:237-270). QtSpim and the CLI both do this.
findings.evidence: Code comparison.
findings.suggested_resolution: Optionally copy ProcessInfo.environment (deterministic order) in upstream layout; document if it is intentionally omitted for privacy or determinism.
findings.validation: Fixture printing argc, argv and the first envp entries with `env -i FOO=bar` on both implementations.

findings.title: sbrk failure raises MIPS exception 7 instead of SPIM's error path
findings.trigger: sbrk with a negative a0, or past -ldata.
findings.actual: AccessError.exception(7) → the handler prints '[Bad data address]' and execution continues with $v0 unchanged.
findings.expected: expand_data reports 'Can't expand data segment…' plus run_error 'Use -ldata…' (mem.cpp:187-197), which aborts the run in the CLI (longjmp, spim.cpp:890-904). In QtSpim it shows an error dialog.
findings.evidence: Code comparison.
findings.suggested_resolution: Fault with the upstream message (and stderr/Messages output) rather than a guest exception.
findings.validation: Compare-memory-layout case requesting more than -ldata.

findings.title: CLI and app flag semantics differ: positional file plus args, and -asm/-bare changing the pseudo flag
findings.trigger: `swiftspim-cli prog.s arg1`, or `swiftspim-cli -nopseudo -asm -file p.s`.
findings.actual: arg1 is read as a second source file (error). -asm sets acceptPseudoInstructions=true, overriding an earlier -nopseudo; -bare sets it false.
findings.expected: Upstream treats a non-dash argument as the program file followed by program arguments (spim.cpp:219-235; QtSpim main.cpp:186-190). -asm/-bare do not touch accept_pseudo_insts (spim.cpp:164-172; QtSpim main.cpp:133-141).
findings.evidence: Code comparison. Note: upstream's later argument re-parsing has its own quirk, so argv[0] behavior should be decided deliberately.
findings.suggested_resolution: Treat the first positional argument like -file and stop option parsing; leave the pseudo flag alone in -asm/-bare (bare already blocks pseudos).
findings.validation: CLI flag-matrix tests.

findings.title: Run/Step disabled after exit or fault; Abort at a breakpoint continues instead of restarting
findings.trigger: Let a program exit, then press Run. Or Abort at a breakpoint, then Run.
findings.actual: Run is disabled until a reload or Clear Registers. After Abort, Run continues from the current PC.
findings.expected: QtSpim restarts at the start address with a fresh stack when status is STOPPED and not force_break, which covers both a finished program and Abort (menu.cpp:299-307, 372-374, 395). Memory is not reloaded.
findings.evidence: Documented at usermanual.md:59, but it is a functional divergence.
findings.suggested_resolution: Allow Run from halted, fault or aborted states: reset pc, re-run configureStack and keep memory, as upstream does.
findings.validation: UI test: exit → Run reruns from __start; Abort → Run restarts.

findings.title: Data view and exported log only list written bytes; .space/sbrk regions and zero-filled segments are omitted
findings.line: 402-418 (rows built from machine.memory keys), 487-489 (export uses the same rows)
findings.trigger: `.data; buf: .space 64` without writing it, then view Data or Save Log.
findings.actual: buf's rows are absent unless navigated to manually, and the exported Data section omits them.
findings.expected: QtSpim's data window and log print the user data segment range up to data_top, collapsing zero runs, plus stack and kernel data (datawin.cpp; menu.cpp:136-141 exports the window text).
findings.evidence: Partly documented (usermanual.md:208); the export divergence is not documented.
findings.suggested_resolution: Render segment ranges [DATA_BOT, heap), [sp, STACK_TOP) and [K_DATA_BOT, kernelDataTop) with zero-run compression, matching QtSpim's format.
findings.validation: Export comparison against QtSpim's saved log for a .space fixture.

findings.title: Console and data panes rebuild O(n) structures on every refresh; byte-per-entry dictionaries for memory
findings.line: 322-325 (whole output as one Text, onChange compares full strings); Debugger.swift 402-418 (sorts all memory keys per render); Machine.swift 19 ([UInt32: UInt8] memory)
findings.trigger: A program printing several MB, or one touching millions of bytes, run in the GUI.
findings.actual: Every 100 ms refresh re-lays out the full console text and re-sorts every memory key. Memory use grows by dozens of bytes per guest byte.
findings.expected: Responsive UI comparable to QtSpim's QTextEdit append model.
findings.evidence: Code reading; magnitude not measured.
findings.suggested_resolution: Append-only console storage (e.g. NSTextView/AttributedString chunks with a cap), cached and segmented data rows, and a page-based memory backing store.
findings.validation: Profile with a 5 MB output fixture and a 16 MB memory-fill fixture.

findings.title: Hidden 'Append newline' setting still applies outside MMIO mode
findings.trigger: Turn off Append newline in MMIO mode, switch MMIO off, reload, and answer read_int.
findings.actual: The toggle is hidden, but sendInput still omits the newline, so read_int waits indefinitely and there is no visible cause.
findings.expected: Syscall input completes per line.
findings.evidence: Code reading.
findings.suggested_resolution: Force a newline when not in MMIO mode, or always show the toggle.
findings.validation: UI or unit test of sendInput in both modes.

findings.title: 'File I/O as in QtSpim' claim overstates parity
findings.trigger: Guest code that uses fd 0/1/2 with read/write/close, hard-coded fds, or reads/writes larger than 4 MiB.
findings.actual: fds are virtual and start at 3. fd 0 reads the console, and fd 1/2 write to the console. close(0/1/2) returns -1. Counts above 4,194,304 return -1.
findings.expected: Upstream passes guest fds straight to host open/read/write/close (syscall.cpp:189-228).
findings.evidence: Source comparison. The Swift choices are reasonable but undocumented.
findings.suggested_resolution: Document these deliberate deviations, or match upstream where safe.
findings.validation: Doc review; fixtures for fd 1 write and large reads.

findings.title: Text listing and export enumerate only assembled addresses; code written at runtime to empty text words is never shown
findings.line: 397-401 (instructions from image.instructions); Machine.swift 304-306 creates new code entries
findings.trigger: A self-modifying program stores an instruction word into an unassembled .text slot (e.g. after `.space`).
findings.actual: The new instruction executes but is absent from the Text pane and the exported log. Modified words show their original source comment.
findings.expected: QtSpim's text window renders the live text segment, regenerated on text_modified (mem.cpp:53, 484).
findings.evidence: Code reading; QtSpim textwin rendering not traced line by line in this review.
findings.suggested_resolution: Expose Machine's live code map for listing and export, and mark rows modified at runtime.
findings.validation: Self-modifying fixture; check the listing and log contents.

remaining_coverage_gaps: Read-only review: nothing was built, run, or timed. No finding was confirmed by execution, and the .build/*.log validation claims were not independently checked.

AssemblerOpcodes.swift (opcode/spec table) and Tests/SpimCoreTests/SpimCoreTests.swift were not read line by line. Pseudo-instruction expansions were spot-checked against inst.cpp/parser.y only where noted, not exhaustively (e.g. numeric branch targets, `(expr)>>n` immediates, gp-relative .extern/.lcomm forms, ulh/ush/rol/ror sequences in big-endian).

The disassembly text format was not compared with upstream inst_to_string/print_inst; QtSpim textwin/datawin/regwin rendering, the exact log format and FP register window fields were not compared in detail.

Timer/interrupt timing (upstream checks interrupts only per run_spim chunk / IO_INTERVAL, not every instruction) and timer.s/time.s/read.s behavior were not evaluated; those fixtures are not used by any test or script.
Big-endian mode has no upstream oracle; endian-specific paths (lwl/lwr/swl/swr, li.d, doubles, MMIO) were reviewed only by reading.

SwiftUI lifecycle concerns not verified: whether Console window onDisappear at app quit removes .console from saved panels; whether Xcode-injected launch arguments (e.g. -NSDocumentRevisionsDebugMode YES) are treated as files by Debugger.launch (Debugger.swift:537-543); main-thread blocking if a guest opens a FIFO in unrestricted host-file mode.

No tests exist for: semantic-error recovery, cross-file forward references, breakpoint plus input interaction, Debugger.sendInput/run/load(keepState) logic, CLI flag parsing, exception message output, non-UTF-8 I/O, sbrk failure, MMIO interrupt-driven output, or relocation of the CLI binary.

Upstream quirks (e.g. spim.cpp re-assigning program_argv for each later non-dash argument, QtSpim state.cpp saving 'CommandLine' but reading 'CommandLineArguments') were noted but not treated as parity requirements.
